steps.title: Prepare particle suspension
steps.instruction: Make a 1 % w/v aqueous suspension of polystyrene‑chrome‑oxide core‑shell microparticles (Spherotec CFM‑1000‑5, 102 µm diameter or CFM‑40‑10, 4.67 µm diameter) that are coated with 11‑carbon‑long hydrocarbon ligands terminating in a carboxyl group.

steps.title: Deposit suspension on glass
steps.instruction: Pre‑heat a 2.5 × 7.5 cm glass substrate on a hot plate to ~60 °C for a few minutes. Pipette drops of the suspension onto the substrate at equal distances, allowing each drop to evaporate before adding the next, until a granular film of ~1 cm radius is formed. Keep the drop spacing large enough to permit easy washing later.

steps.title: Plasma‑etch exposed ligands
steps.instruction: Place the particle‑coated glass into a Diener PICO UHP plasma asher. Set the device to 50 % power (100 W) with a 50 % oxygen gas mixture and run for 10 min. This removes the ligands from the particle hemispheres facing upward while the side in contact with the glass retains its ligands.

steps.title: Magnetize particles
steps.instruction: Position the dried particles on the glass within a perpendicular magnetic field of approximately 2500 Oersted generated by an electromagnet. This aligns the ferromagnetic spins on the ligand‑free hemisphere, fixing the magnetization direction of all particles.

steps.title: Wash and collect Janus particles
steps.instruction: Wash the particles off the glass substrate into a piece of filter paper, then retrieve the Janus particles from the filter.
